Definition: literally a failure of flesh, i.e. emaciation; figuratively, hypocrisy
BiblicalUsage: Kachash is the lying of the flesh — leanness and hypocrisy, the body failing and the tongue denying. Hosea says Israel ate the fruit of lies; Job says his leanness bears witness against him; and the psalmist asks God to catch the wicked in the cursing and lying that they speak.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word ties the body to the tongue: lies make a people lean, and hypocrisy wastes us from the inside. Truth is not only right — it is nourishing, and that is why I want to live on it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
